statement: Carbon-14 birth dating of human cardiomyocytes shows renewal at roughly one per cent a year at age 25, falling below half a per cent by age 75, so fewer than half of the cardiomyocytes in a heart are replaced over a lifetime.

measurement.assay: carbon-14 birth dating from atmospheric bomb-pulse
measurement.effect: about 1% per year at 25, under 0.5% at 75

replication.note: One group's method, later refined; the order of magnitude is not disputed.

limitations: turnover measured across the whole heart, not in an infarct border zone

provenance.method: manual reasoning from the cited sources' abstracts (Crossref/Europe PMC), checked 2026-09-14; no source opened at figure level
